patch.value:
CodeRabbit, Security & Privacy / Minor, scripts/shell-command-scan.ts:634-637 (PR 84):

"**Normalize YAML block-scalar indentation before scanning.** — `publishInvocationsIn` passes workflow text directly to `shellScalars`, which only removes leading tabs for `<<-`. YAML indentation remains in the source text, so a valid heredoc terminator can remain active in the scanner. The scanner then skips later assignments and can miss a variable-based publish.

Normalize workflow block indentation before scanning. Add an audit regression with an indented terminator, `NPM=npm`, and \$NPM publish after it."

CodeRabbit's follow-up: "The YAML indentation check should confirm the exact input passed to `shellScalars`. If indentation remains, the assignment rule must accept the YAML block indentation without accepting non-standalone shell syntax."
YAML run-block indentation reaches shellScalars undedented, so a heredoc terminator written inside a run block never ends its payload

CodeRabbit Security/Minor on PR 84: publishInvocationsIn passes workflow text to shellScalars with the YAML block indentation attached, and the heredoc terminator is the one whitespace-sensitive rule — a real terminator never matches and later assignments stay unindexed.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
Determined by reading the path and by measurement, not assertion. publishInvocationsIn passes source.text (the raw file) through joinContinuations to shellScalars — no dedent anywhere. Pattern audit over every whitespace-sensitive rule: STANDALONE_ASSIGNMENT opens with ^[ \t]* and tolerates the indentation; control closers and function openers are matched against code.trim(); a comment starts after any of [\s;&|(){}] so leading whitespace qualifies; bashArrays anchors on (?:^|\s); heredoc START detection is a character scan. Exactly ONE rule is defeated: the heredoc terminator comparison (candidate === delimiter on the whole line). Inside a run: | block a real terminator therefore never matches, the heredoc swallows the rest of the file, every later assignment is payload, and a $NPM publish after it is omitted while an attested sibling satisfies the non-vacuity guard. Measured end to end: the realistic run-block fixture returned failures: 0 before the fix (clean over an unattested publish) and failures: 1 after; the same text hand-dedented always returned 1.

Fix: dedentRunBlocks(text), applied in publishInvocationsIn for files matching the workflow/action YAML paths only. It learns each run: block's indentation from its first non-blank line (as YAML does), strips exactly that prefix, keeps deeper indentation, ends the block at the first non-blank line indented less, and only run: keys are treated as blocks (a block scalar under any other key is data no shell runs). A plain shell script is deliberately NOT dedented: its indentation is the shell's own, and bash does not accept an indented terminator without <<- — so a whitespace-tolerant terminator comparison or an ungated dedent would index payload prose as a scalar (the opposite error), which the scripts/release.sh regression rejects.

value.note: run-block bypass regression and plain-script guard

value.command: npm test -- --test-name-pattern "a run-block heredoc terminator ends the payload, so later assignments are indexed"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "an indented heredoc terminator in a plain shell script is not a terminator"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "run-block content is dedented the way YAML delivers it to bash"
npm test -- --test-name-pattern "run-block dedenting refuses shapes YAML would not deliver as blocks"

patch.value: dedentRunBlocks learns each run: block's indentation from its first non-blank line as YAML does, strips exactly that prefix, keeps deeper indentation, ends the block at the first less-indented non-blank line, and treats only run: keys as blocks. publishInvocationsIn applies it for .github/workflows and composite-action paths, because that is where YAML hands bash dedented text; a plain shell script keeps its own indentation, and an indented terminator there is not a terminator in bash - the opposite error is guarded by the scripts/release.sh regression.

The run-block bypass regression must fail (one failure naming the missing flag) when the terminator is not recognised and pass after; its positive assertion (a post-terminator FLAG carries the attestation, zero failures) must fail when the terminator is not recognised; the plain-shell regression must fail if terminator matching is made whitespace-tolerant anywhere; the two dedent unit tests must fail if the dedent is removed.

Revert-proof by hand: reverting the dedent to identity reddened exactly the run-block bypass test and both dedent unit tests together with the heredoc tests (92 pass / 5 fail); making the terminator comparison whitespace-tolerant reddened exactly the plain-shell guard test (89 pass / 1 fail). Restored: 357/357, npm run coverage 100/100/100, npm run check, npm run docstring, npm run release:check all green, and the repository's own gate verify-release-publish-attestation passes on the real workflows. pm test --run collides with this repository's own pm-integration tests inside the linked-test sandbox (pre-existing, files untouched by this change); every linked command was executed directly and observed green, including single-title runs.

Confirmed by reading the path and by measurement: no dedent exists between publishInvocationsIn and shellScalars, the heredoc terminator is the single whitespace-sensitive rule, and a realistic run-block fixture measured failures 0 (clean over an unattested publish) before the fix and failures 1 after. Fixed with dedentRunBlocks applied to workflow-path sources only.
